title: Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency Act of 2018
official_summary:
Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency Act of 2018

(Sec. 2) This bill amends the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to redesignate the Department of Homeland Security's (DHS's) National Protection and Programs Directorate as the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency. It transfers resources and responsibilities of the directorate to the agency.

The agency shall be headed by the Director of National Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security. Its responsibilities shall include: leading cybersecurity and critical infrastructure security programs, operations, and associated policy; and carrying out DHS's responsibilities concerning chemical facility antiterrorism standards.

The bill details the organizational structure of the agency.

(Sec. 3) The bill transfers within DHS the Office of Biometric Identity Management to the Management Directorate.

It also requires DHS to transfer the Federal Protective Service to an appropriate DHS component, directorate, or office following the completion of an ongoing Government Accountability Office review.

(Sec. 4) DHS shall report on its leadership role in cloud-based cybersecurity deployments for civilian federal departments and agencies.

summary.headline: This law creates the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency inside the Department of Homeland Security by renaming and reorganizing an existing directorate.
summary.what_it_does: The law changes the name of the Department of Homeland Security's National Protection and Programs Directorate to the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency. The new agency takes over the directorate's resources and duties, and it is led by a Director of National Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security. Its duties include leading cybersecurity and critical infrastructure security programs and enforcing chemical facility antiterrorism standards. The law also moves the Office of Biometric Identity Management to the department's Management Directorate and requires the department to move the Federal Protective Service after a pending Government Accountability Office review. Finally, it requires a report on the department's role in cloud-based cybersecurity for federal civilian agencies.

who_it_affects.group: Owners and operators of chemical facilities
who_it_affects.how: They fall under chemical facility antiterrorism standards that the new agency is responsible for carrying out.

who_it_affects.group: Owners and operators of critical infrastructure
who_it_affects.how: The new agency leads federal cybersecurity and critical infrastructure security programs that cover them.
They are covered by the department's reported role in cloud-based cybersecurity deployments.

who_it_affects.group: Federal Protective Service employees and contractors
who_it_affects.how: The service will be moved to another part of the department after the Government Accountability Office review is finished.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted on November 16, 2018, and the Federal Protective Service move depends on completing the ongoing Government Accountability Office review.
